findings.desc: CHK-015:edge:1 (matcher count bound is policy-resolved, not hardcoded): no fixture in red-w2d-rejection-matrix.mjs or the smoke validates the matcher-count bound under a policy with a DIFFERENT policy.maxMatchers value. Every other floor claim of this kind in the same story (rule-2 length/entropy floors in red-w2d-specificity-conjunction.mjs via a raised-minMatcherLen policy, the class registry in CHK-016 via a CUSTOM matcherClassRegistry, policyDigest content-sensitivity in CHK-010 via an otherPolicy) IS proven with a two-policy differential; only the CHK-015 count bound is proven solely against the frozen default (maxMatchers=8), so a hard-coded 8 in place of policy.maxMatchers would pass every committed test. The binder self-flagged this exact gap in its own evidence note.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed: two-policy differential added - an identical 4-matcher envelope is accepted at maxMatchers=8 and rejected at 3, with the message asserted to carry policy.maxMatchers=3, so a hard-coded 8 can no longer pass.

findings.desc: CHK-012 read-only claim (packages/main/tests/red/red-w2d-command-readonly.mjs, packages/main/src/tasks/red-evidence-envelope-smoke.ts section 7): the handler doc comment on red_evidence_envelope_check (packages/main/src/handlers/red-evidence.ts ~line 349) asserts the command spawns no RED run and its only child processes are the W2b binding readers git rev-parse/git show. No committed test verifies this: the mechanism used (a per-file SHA-256 snapshot of .lattice/ taken before and after the call) can only detect writes under .lattice/; it does not intercept, mock, or otherwise observe child_process.spawn/exec/spawnSync calls, so a regression that caused the handler to shell out to run a test (e.g. code drifted toward the reserved-for-later runner leaf) would pass this regression undetected even though it violates the storys core before a run is ever spent safety property. Given this is the single most safety-critical claim of the whole command, the read-only regression should intercept/spy on child_process to positively prove no RED-run-shaped spawn occurs, not rely solely on directory-hash absence-of-evidence.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed together with F-012 and F-013 (same defect, three hosts converged). The snapshot claim is narrowed to exactly what it proves, AND a child_process recorder now asserts the real spawn set. The recorder falsified the old docstring enumeration: repository/worktree resolution also runs git rev-parse --show-toplevel, --git-common-dir and git worktree list --porcelain beyond the W2b rev-parse/show. All read-only; the git read is untouched and the docstring's narrow claim (spawns no RED run) was not weakened.

findings.desc: CHK-013:happy:0 literal intent text reads: red-evidence-envelope-smoke.ts listed in lattice.config.json validate.commands and lattice validate runs it successfully. The bound evidence (packages/main/tests/red/red-w2c-validate-registration.mjs) only statically enumerates dist/tasks/red-evidence-* on disk and cross-checks it against the validate.commands array in config; it never invokes the lattice validate command itself. CHK-013:happy:1 separately runs the smoke by direct node invocation (node packages/main/dist/tasks/red-evidence-envelope-smoke.js), not through the lattice validate pipeline. So no committed evidence in this story exercises the actual validate-pipeline invocation path (spawn args/cwd/timeout handling for this entry) end to end; the binder self-flagged this exact gap (lattice validate was not run for this binding). Registration-in-config + direct-invocation-passes only jointly approximate the literal intent, and this exact substitution pattern was previously used for the same reason in W2c (red-w2c-validate-registration.mjs), so it is a known, repeated, but still real gap against the literal command the intent names.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed: red-w2d-command-readonly section 8 now resolves the entry via configuredValidationCommands and executes it through runValidationCommand - the two functions lattice validate itself uses - asserting exit 0, instead of only checking config registration statically.

findings.desc: CHK-002 closed-enum rejections (stream, polarity, greenExempt legality) and CHK-001 identity/kind rejections are exercised only against kind:literal-line matchers across red-w2d-rejection-matrix.mjs and the smoke; no fixture asserts an invalid stream, invalid polarity, or illegal greenExempt on a kind:class matcher. In envelope.ts these checks (validateAssertionEnvelope lines ~317-337) run unconditionally before the kind-specific branch, so the current implementation is not actually kind-differentiated, but the committed matrix does not prove that: a future change that moved these checks inside the literal-line-only branch (mirroring how value-byte-length checks are correctly literal-line-only) would silently stop rejecting a malformed class matcher stream/polarity/greenExempt, and no committed test would catch it.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed: the full closed-enum table (5 streams, 4 polarities, greenExempt x3, duplicate id across kinds) is re-run against kind:'class' matchers, each rejection asserted by code.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/red-evidence/envelope.ts:346-348 (matcher-value-empty) tags an EMPTY literal-line value as R1-3. Spec places non-emptiness under §1.3 rule 1 ("value MUST be stored trimmed (§1.1.1), MUST be non-empty, and MUST NOT be a member of policy.forbiddenCatchAlls", spec:401-403), which is the §1.3 minimum-specificity rule that R1-2 owns ("a degenerate/blocklisted literal", spec:495-498). R1-3s own enumerated list (spec:499-504) explicitly names only value longer than maxMatcherLen or carrying leading/trailing whitespace for value-bound failures — it never mentions empty/too-short. The codebase itself already applies this exact reasoning to the two sibling clauses of the same rule-1 triple: trimmed -> R1-3 (explicitly named in R1-3s list) and blocklisted -> R1-2 (explicitly named in R1-2s list, per envelope.ts:393-400). non-empty is the third clause and is NOT named in R1-3s list, so by the codes own established methodology it should route to R1-2 like blocklisted, not R1-3 like trimmed. Failing input: matchers:[{id:L1,kind:literal-line,value:"",stream:combined,polarity:present-in-red}] -> current output tags matcher-value-empty as R1-3; expected R1-2 per §1.3 rule 1. This choice is pinned into 3 committed regressions (red-w2d-rejection-matrix.mjs:219-221, red-evidence-envelope-smoke.ts:298), so it is a systematic mistag, not a slip.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed together with F-006 (same defect, behavior lane and codex host-B converged). An empty literal moved out of the bounds layer into the section 1.3 block and is now tagged R1-2. The argument that settled it: the code already split the other two clauses of the same rule-1 triple correctly - trimmed to R1-3 because R1-3's enumeration names it, blocklisted to R1-2 because R1-2's does - and 'non-empty' is absent from R1-3's enumeration, so it routes to R1-2 by the module's own existing logic.

findings.desc: [codex host-B #2, orchestrator-verified] An empty literal value is tagged R1-3 but the spec assigns it R1-2. Section 1.6's R1-3 trigger enumeration covers a value LONGER than maxMatcherLen or carrying leading/trailing whitespace - it does not cover an empty value. Section 1.3 rule 1 explicitly requires value to be non-empty, and rule-1 failures are R1-2. red-w2d-rejection-matrix.mjs currently pins the wrong tag, which freezes the error. Fix the tag and the fixture.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed - see B-9ff1:F-005, the same defect reported independently by codex host-B. Empty literal now tagged R1-2; the matrix fixture that pinned the wrong tag was corrected too, since a fixture pinning a wrong tag freezes the error.

findings.desc: [codex host-B #4, orchestrator-verified against spec text] greenExempt:false on a non-present-in-red matcher is accepted; it must reject. Section 1.1 states greenExempt is 'legal ONLY on polarity present-in-red matchers (any other polarity CARRYING IT is rejected)' - the test is whether the field is PRESENT, not whether it is true. The implementer's documented ambiguity resolution 5 reasoned that false cannot change assertion identity under section 0.4 and therefore accepted it; that reasoning is wrong on this clause. Reject on presence regardless of value, and add the fixture.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed: the guard is now presence-based (else if polarity !== 'present-in-red'), matching section 1.1's 'any other polarity CARRYING IT is rejected' - the test is whether the field is present, not whether it is true. The implementer's earlier ambiguity note reasoning from section 0.4 identity was wrong on this clause and the header note was rewritten.

findings.desc: [codex host-B #5, orchestrator-verified] testCaseRef is never matched against the adapter's registered testCaseRefPattern. Section 1.2 (argv resolution) states: match testCaseRef against testCaseRefPattern; no match rejects R1-5. This is envelope-decidable - the pattern lives in the resolved policy registry and the testCaseRef is in the envelope - so it belongs in the same R1-5 check that already validates adapter registration. Failing input: adapterId npm-script@1 with testCaseRef 'free-form:not-derived' currently returns ok:true.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed: testCaseRef is now matched against the resolved adapter's testCaseRefPattern, no match rejecting R1-5 per section 1.2 argv resolution. Six pattern-mismatch fixtures plus a cross-adapter row where the same ref is rejected under node-test@1 and accepted under npm-script@1.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/red-evidence/envelope.ts:274-434: the matcherSetEvaluable gate (line 385, requiring rawMatchers.length in [1,maxMatchers] AND bounded.length>0) suppresses the ENTIRE §1.3 block — per-matcher rule1/2 AND the rule-3 class-only-present-in-red check — whenever the matcher COUNT is out of bounds. This contradicts the modules own documented invariant at envelope.ts:236-237 ("Every check runs — nothing short-circuits — so co-occurring faults are ALL reported and no tag suppresses another"). Concrete failing input verified against dist: an envelope with 9 matchers (policy.maxMatchers=8) where the sole present-in-red matcher is a class matcher (stderr-nonempty) and the other 8 are valid present-in-green literals — this genuinely violates §1.3 rule 3 (a class matcher can never be the sole present-in-red evidence, spec:411-414, tag R1-2) in addition to the count-bound R1-3. validateAssertionEnvelope returns ONLY [{tag:R1-3,code:matcher-count-above-maximum}] — the R1-2 rule-3 violation is silently dropped, never surfaced to the operator. Verified by direct probe against packages/main/dist/core/red-evidence/envelope.js (matches src at HEAD). R1-1 is unaffected (computed independently, still fires alongside R1-3 when co-occurring — confirmed by a second probe), so this is specific to the R1-2 §1.3 block. None of the 3 committed regressions (red-w2d-rejection-matrix.mjs, red-w2d-specificity-conjunction.mjs, red-evidence-envelope-smoke.ts) construct an over/under-count fixture that ALSO carries a rule1/2/3 violation, so the gap is untested as well as unimplemented.

[codex host-B #6, orchestrator-verified] Absolute-path detection recognizes only a leading slash. Section 1.1.3 requires targetArtifactRef to be slash-normalized AND RELATIVE, rejecting an absolute path at envelope schema time as R1-3. Failing input: targetArtifactRef 'C:/outside' is slash-normalized and absolute yet returns ok:true. Reject non-relative forms generally, not just the POSIX leading-slash form.

[codex host-B #7, orchestrator-verified] supplementaryArtifact:null is treated as absent. Section 0.4 states every optional field is OMITTED entirely when absent and is NEVER written as null or empty string, so an explicit null is a malformed envelope rather than an omission. Failing input: supplementaryArtifact:null returns ok:true; it must reject.

[codex host-B #8 CONVERGED with test-coverage F-002] The read-only regression cannot prove what it claims. Its mechanism is a before/after SHA-256 snapshot of .lattice/, which detects writes there and nothing else; it never intercepts child_process, so it cannot detect a spawned process. ORCHESTRATOR ADJUDICATION: the handler DOES spawn git via the W2b committed-binding reader (target-bindings.ts runGit uses spawnSync), and that is CORRECT and deliberate - reading the binding from the committed tree rather than the live directory is W2b's anti-swap property. The DEV handoff's phrase 'no process spawning' was too absolute and is not a code defect. What must be fixed is the EVIDENCE: either narrow the claim to what the snapshot proves (no writes under .lattice, no chain record, no gate change) or genuinely assert the spawn set. Do not remove the git read.

packages/main/tests/red/red-w2d-command-readonly.mjs:126-141 and packages/main/src/tasks/red-evidence-envelope-smoke.ts:386-398: the committed read-only proof snapshots per-file SHA-256 hashes of the .lattice tree before/after invoking red_evidence_envelope_check, plus static registry-flag assertions (ownershipClass readOnly, READ_ONLY_COMMANDS membership). Neither technique can detect an errant child-process spawn that writes nothing under .lattice (e.g. outside the repo, to a temp dir, or a network call) — a directory hash and a static classification flag are not behavioral evidence against process spawning. This is a test-assurance gap, not a functional defect: direct source reading confirms the only child processes in the call path are the two read-only git commands (rev-parse/show) inside readCommittedTargetBindings (packages/main/src/core/red-evidence/target-bindings.ts:141,172,180), and the handlers own docstring (packages/main/src/handlers/red-evidence.ts:347-355) correctly and narrowly claims spawns no RED run rather than an absolute spawns nothing claim. Flagging per the review brief item 4 (a test that only hashes a directory cannot detect a process spawn) so the gap between what is claimed and what the regression can actually detect is on record; no code change is indicated, only stronger test assurance (e.g. intercepting child_process.spawn/spawnSync during the check() calls and asserting only git rev-parse/show occur) would close it.
